newsitem.title: UK: New Hanson pretax profit $431.7 million.
newsitem.headline: New Hanson pretax profit $431.7 million.

text.p: The new Hanson Plc, a building materials group left over from the company's four-way splitup, Thursday reported first-half pretax profits of 262.8 million pounds ($431.7 million), which included a five-month contribution from the former Energy Group division.

The continuing operations operating profit for Hanson's remaining building businesses was 69.6 million pounds ($114 million) in the six months ended March 31, compared with 66.3 million ($109 million) in the same period the previous year. Analysts said this gave a more accurate picture of the group's progress.
The group also took the chance to announce that Chairman Lord Hanson will step down at the end of 1997, to be succeeded by Chistopher Collins, the current deputy chairman.
Lord Hanson, founder of the once-mighty conglomerate, said the outlook for the building materials group was bright.

"The signs of improvement in the U.K. housing and construction markets are now more evident, the prospects for our U.S. businesses are good and we look forward to making steady progress during the rest of 1997."
He said the division, spanning building materials and construction, had made "solid progress" in the first half.

The net debt of the group was 325 million pounds ($535 million), up from 174 million ($286 million). This excludes the 125 million ($206 million) in cash received in April from the sale of Hanson Electrical and the 78 million ($128 million) cost of buying Concrete Pipe & Products.
Hanson's U.S. shares fell 50 cents to $26.25 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
